(women's volleyball) |sport16 = Windsurfing }} '''Göztepe Spor Kulübü''' ({{IPA|tr|ɟœztepe spoɾ kulyby}}, Göztepe Sports Club), commonly referred to as Göztepe, is a Turkish multi-sport club based in the [[Göztepe, Konak|Göztepe]] and [[Güzelyalı Bridge|Güzelyalı]] neighborhoods of [[İzmir]]. Founded on 14 June 1925 as '''Göztepe Gençlik Kulübü''' (Göztepe Youth Club), it is one of the oldest sports institutions in [[Turkey]] with a rich history spanning over a century.{{cite web |title=Göztepe celebrates 100th anniversary |url=https://www.fanatik.com.tr/goztepe-100-yasinda-2512312 |website=Fanatik |language=tr |date=14 June 2025}} Originally formed as a neighborhood club, Göztepe became nationally prominent in the mid-20th century, particularly after becoming Turkish champions in 1950.{{cite web |title=Göztepe: Türkiye Şampiyonu |url=https://www.ntvspor.net/tarihde-bugun/goztepe-1950-sampiyonlugu |website=NTV Spor |language=tr |date=6 June 2020}} In 1969, the club made history by becoming the first [[Turkey|Turkish]] team to reach the semi-finals of a [[UEFA competitions|European competition]], achieving this milestone in the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] (a predecessor to the [[UEFA Europa League]]).{{cite web |title=Göztepe: First Turkish semi-finalist in Europe |url=https://www.uefa.com/insideuefa/news/0264-10f9d58b0cc2-9b9d5e4e6dd7-1000/ |website=UEFA.com |access-date=26 July 2025}} Besides football, the club operates as a [[Joint-stock company|joint-stock company (AŞ)]] and includes multiple branches in [[fencing]], [[triathlon]], [[handball]], [[volleyball]], [[basketball]], [[gymnastics]], [[archery]], [[Cue sports|billiards]], [[sailing (sport)|sailing]], [[swimming (sport)|swimming]], and [[windsurfing]], making it one of the most comprehensive sports institutions in the country.{{cite web |title=Göztepe Sports Club branches |url=https://www.goztepe.org.tr/Kurumsal/Spor-Dallari/1 |website=goztepe.org.tr |access-date=26 July 2025}} Despite facing relegation and financial hardship between 2002 and 2008, Göztepe maintained one of the most loyal fan bases in [[Turkey]]. Even during their time in the [[Turkish Regional Amateur League]], the club continued to attract higher average attendances than many top-flight clubs.{{cite web |title=Göztepe draws record crowds in amateur league |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/amator-ligde-sampiyon-ama-stadyum-doluyor-30013854 |website=Hürriyet |language=tr |date=12 May 2008}} Their resilience and support culminated in a return to the [[Süper Lig]], where they continue to compete under the ownership of [[Sport Republic]] and the leadership of [[Rasmus Ankersen]]. As of the [[2024–25 Süper Lig|2024–25 season]], Göztepe competes in the [[Süper Lig]], and currently ranks 8th out of 19 teams in the league table. In the '''"all-time table"''' of [[Football in Turkey|Turkish football]], Göztepe holds the 13th place overall based on historic performance and points."}}
